utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Tieger, there was an outstanding question yesterday about the date of a certain transcript. Could you inform the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm afraid at this point I have nothing to add. I certainly thought about it last night after we recessed, but due to the hour I was unable to -- both sides of our adjournment, that is last night and this morning, it was either too late or too early to get a meaningful response. I have that at the top of the list, and I will attempt to provide the court with an answer as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I do understand that you're dependent on other people to inform you. If you are paying attention to those transcripts, perhaps you could also pay attention to the following: In the transcript -- because I could read them without being dependent on anyone yesterday evening. In the transcript of a conversation of the 11th of December, 1991, between Mr. Bajagic and Mr. Karadzic -- well, first of all, the transcript says that all pages are page 5 out of 5, which is at least not of great assistance if we want to refer to certain pages. But the last two pages, 5 out of 5, I found, at least at the last page, but certainly the last page, all the speakers are mixed up. If you read them, and if you read the text, "Well, good, Mr. Radovan," and if the speaker is supposed to be Mr. Karadzic himself, or when you read "goodbye, my Zvonko, regards," and the speaker is Zvonko Bajagic, then that urges us to compare the English text with the original, and then it seems to me that all speakers -- well, the two speakers have been, at least on the last page, constantly mixed up. So the Chamber would ask you two things. First of all, to provide a copy which reflects the original in B/C/S. That's one. And the second request is that the material before presented to the Chamber is checked on this kind of points, because it's not the first time that these kinds of things happened, and the Chamber would rather concentrate on the content than on checking how to explain the parts of the documents that are really incomprehensible, if not compared to the original and if not corrected properly. So then the Chamber will hear from you, and I take it that we get a few other pages, whether 5 out of 5, or 4 out of 5, that's another matter. Having dealt with that, and inviting Ms. Loukas not to complicate matters to a level not understandable any more for the witness -- I'm not saying that it was, but there was at least a risk that the exercise might lead to more confusion than to more clarification. I'd like to ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I'd agree, Your Honour. Simplicity is always a virtue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Redzic. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. From your answer, I do take it that you can hear me. May I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Ms. Loukas will now continue. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Loukas: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you'll recall that when we finished yesterday evening I was asking you some questions about your awareness of the Cutileiro plan. Are you having problems with your headphones?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It seems that the witness does not...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not hear you before. I did not hear the first part of your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Mr. Redzic. I'll just repeat that. You'll recall that when we finished yesterday evening, I was asking you some questions about the Cutileiro plan.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just one final question on that topic. I take it, of course, that you're aware that Izetbegovic had agreed to the principles of the Cutileiro plan but had then changed his mind. You're aware of that; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it in the papers and I watched some of those things on TV. I'm not aware of any details. I only knew what I saw on TV. I didn't know the truth of the matter, because I did not see anything on paper. I did not see any documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's, of course, a similar position that you adopt in relation to your awareness of the SDS activities, of course, at a senior level?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't go into that. I wouldn't speak about the SDS or the SDA or any other government. I was not informed about any of those things, and I would not wish to talk about things that I knew only superficially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Mr. Redzic. And what I want to take you to is awareness of some matters of the local community in Vlasenica. Are you with me? That's the next topic I want to go to.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which local commune are you referring to? Are you referring to the municipality of Vlasenica --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- or a local commune?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. The local municipality of Vlasenica. So we're on the same page; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So we are talking about Vlasenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. At the opstina level, correct. Okay. Now, in September 1991, were you aware of mixed Croat-Muslim paramilitary groups --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem with the headphones. Let's continue. I'll keep a close eye on it. Yes. Perhaps it's better to use another earphone. Mr. Redzic, is it any better now? Is it better now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, not many people are speaking at this moment, but can you hear me at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I hear something from the interpreter, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it a matter of interpretation or is it a matter of earphones? Ms. Cmeric, do you receive any interpretation at this moment if you would choose the B/C/S channel?

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I was on channel 0.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. But could you please change to the B/C/S. And do you receive interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do receive interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So interpretation is not the problem. Mr. Redzic, do you now hear the interpretation of what I'm saying? Yes. You say something, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are interpretations.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to indicate it's breaking up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's breaking up. Then it seems to be a technical problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll try one more earphone. If that doesn't solve the matter, then there will be something wrong with the signal. Mr. Redzic, you made some gestures which I understand gestures of satisfaction of the interpretation you now receive; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Redzic, if you have any further problems with your headphones, please let us know straight away so we can stop and attend to whatever it is, so there's no breakdown in communication. Understood?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, prior to those technical difficulties, I was asking you a question about your awareness or otherwise of certain activities in the Vlasenica municipality. You understood where we were up to so far; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm waiting for your direct questions. What you have just said was very general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly. It's not a question. I just want to ensure that you know where we're up to at this point, okay? Now, were you aware in September 1991 of mixed Croat-Muslim paramilitary groups setting up stake-outs and frisking travellers on the road between Milici and the Boksit mine?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is beyond comprehension, not to know an answer to this question. In my testimony, I said that Vlasenica municipality had 0.01 Croats, so it doesn't make sense to think that there were some joint groups that put up blockades and searched travellers in the areas that you mentioned. In that area, there were just two groups: Serbs and Muslims. As for Croats, there were just 0.01 per cent Croats. They were mostly teachers who had arrived from other areas and worked in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, may I direct you in the following manner: You said that it made no sense to even consider mixed groups. Whether it makes sense or not is, first of all, a matter of reasoning, not a matter of fact. I'm not suggesting that it was the case, but it could be that Croats from elsewhere would have joined. I'm not saying that this is the case, but -- so whether it makes sense or makes no sense is a different matter. Ms. Loukas asked you whether you were aware of any such mixed groups blockading -- blocking the roads. If you are, please tell us. If you are not, please tell us that you are not. Whether it makes sense or not is not something to be discussed at this moment. Also, if you, for example, would know about such groups but not including Croats, just tell us what you know about Muslim groups or whether these were Hungarians or whatever. Tell us what you know and don't discuss whether the question makes any sense or not. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just in relation to that, Mr. Redzic, you do understand that the Judges have to decide this case. You do understand that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And, of course, neither you nor I are going to decide this case.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth will help the Judges decide.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. And, of course, you know that it's the way of justice that it's fair to give both sides a chance to ask questions. You appreciate that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, and that's why I'm here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, getting back to my question. Of course, my question did not contain the inference that I was talking about Croats from the local municipality of Vlasenica. What I'm doing is asking you a series of questions about your awareness about various activities in the local municipality, and most of the questions should be able to be answered yes or no, whether you have an awareness or whether you don't. Are you with me so far?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can add anything on a factual basis, add it, but when you can answer yes, answer yes, and where you can answer no, answer no. Do you understand me? Because we have limited time in this court.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you aware in February 1992 of members of a Muslim and Croat armed paramilitary formation kidnapping people, hijacking trucks, and conducting searches on the road between Milici and the Boksit mine? This is in February 1992 I'm talking about now.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware in February, March, and April of 1992 of some members of the Muslim people in Vlasenica leaving on their own volition for Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware on the 16th of May, 1992, of the disarming of Muslim paramilitary formations in Zaklopaca?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Chamber will allow me to say something about this place. Zaklopaca suffered a disaster at the beginning of the war. 83 civilians were killed, amongst them five or six children. 80 per cent of them were women. The rest were men. So this is not correct. This is a lie, and so many lies were told about Zaklopaca village. On that same day, these people were killed. And I apologise, Your Honours. I had to say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, a question was put to you. It's not up to you to say that there are lies. It was just a question put to you. The question was whether you are aware that there was any disarming of Muslim paramilitary formations on the 16th of May, 1992. If there was, that does not exclude that other people were killed, either prior to that or later to that, and whether this would be part of the truth or the whole truth, or it would be not true at all, is a different question. You're asked whether you are aware of any disarming on the 16th of May, 1992 of Muslim paramilitary formations in that place. Are you aware?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I come back to the previous question put to you. You were asked whether you were aware of any Muslim people leaving Vlasenica in certain month, including the month of April 1992. You said: No, I'm not aware. Did I understand from your previous testimony that -- did I understand from your previous testimony that you yourself left Vlasenica in the month of April 1992, that is to say, on the 18th or the 19th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, a question was put to me whether I was aware that some people left Vlasenica in February and went to Tuzla. This is what I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the question was covering more months.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. It was February, March, and April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question -- and I ask you to carefully listen to the questions. The question was whether you were aware of Muslim people leaving Vlasenica in the month February, March, or April 1992. Since I now I understand that you misunderstood the question, could you please answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mass departure from Vlasenica happened at the beginning of April 1992. At that time, most of the people from Vlasenica went to Kladanj, Tuzla, and Zivinice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And there was another part in the question, a detail. Could you please ask the witness about that, Ms. Loukas. That was about the why, and -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just going back to that previous question. The situation is that in February, March, and April of 1992, members of the Muslim people in Vlasenica left of their own volition for Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I didn't want to cover that disjunctive in the two questions which I think was responsible for some of the confusion we've heard but now it seems counsel is trying to take advantage of it. The original question was did people leave in February March and April, which seemed to suggest an exodus began in February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's clear, Ms. Loukas, that the witness in his answer has emphasised that it was in the beginning of April that the majority -- and I don't know whether we need any details about how many per cent at that moment and whether it was five or several per cent earlier. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour. I think I'll just leave February and March alone and concentrate on April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Redzic, are you aware in April of members of the Muslim community in Vlasenica leaving of their own volition?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not of their own volition. They did leave, but not of their own volition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Redzic, it's true, is it not, that in your evidence yesterday in relation to the question of negotiations over the division of the municipality you indicated that you'd actually spoken to Mr. Izetbegovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have a page reference in the transcript, please. I see counsel is referring to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Loukas, to the extent possible, could you guide us.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. I'm still looking for it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll try to find the page. You may continue, and then -- because it's clearly in my mind that there was some consultation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, Mr. Redzic, I think you referred in the statement you gave on the 12th of October, 1994, that you made contact with President Izetbegovic and that he told you to give the Serbs the impression that you were complying with the order so that you could give as many Muslims as possible the chance to flee the city. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not what it says in my statement. It wasn't stated the way you put it. If I can clarify this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, before you go on to that, I'll just -- so you're saying that you don't agree that what you said in your statement was: "I made contact with President Izetbegovic, who told me to give the Serbs the impression we were complying with the order so we could give as many Muslims as Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond possible the chance to flee the city. I left Vlasenica on 18th of April, 1992." You're telling the Court that that's not what's in your statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think it would be fair and I think it's been the practice in this Chamber to provide the witness with a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 47, line 2 in my transcript, which is the non-corrected transcript -- people out. That's -- no. Yes. That's what -- at least one of the consultations. And I'm -- if you take the transcript of yesterday and search for Izetbegovic, you'll find all the references to -- let me -- I have one on page 47, line 2. I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I find not the specific page reference as far as the people to flee, but I do to get the people out. It's more or less -- it's not exactly, perhaps, but I have to admit that I couldn't find it immediately. If you have it, Ms. Loukas, would you please provide it to us. Otherwise I'll continue to search.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was referring to the statement at that point. Now I'll refer back to the transcript, Your Honours, kindly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise for misunderstanding you. So the transcript would be -- I take it, then, you will go to page 47.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just on this topic, the evidence you gave yesterday was that you spoke with Mr. Izetbegovic, and Mr. Izetbegovic said: "Stall for as long as possible to get the people out. Because the people weren't organised, they didn't have weapons or anything else, they didn't have any possibility of surviving that territory, given what had happened or was happening to the Muslim and Bosniak population." Now, you recall giving that answer yesterday, I take it?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said. I said that because it was a matter of avoiding consequences in the future.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate that. But you would agree with me, Mr. Redzic, that arrangements were undertaken to ensure that Muslims could leave; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's a question I put to you. Why was it necessary for the Muslims to flee? Was it in front of tanks and rifle barrels that were already being put to use and the Bosniak civilian population was being killed? The reason for their departure was their security. It was the fact that they were victims, that property was being destroyed. That's the reason for which that population, those inhabitants, set off in the direction of Tuzla, Kladanj, and other places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Redzic, I hope you'll appreciate both our functions here, and that is that I'm here to ask the questions and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, on the other hand, if I may interrupt. If you just ignore the difference between the words "leave" and "flee," then we'll be in this courtroom for the next hour in great confusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So nevertheless, the situation is that in your conversation with Mr. Izetbegovic, you wanted to ensure that as many Muslims as possible left Vlasenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our concern was to save as many Muslims as possible and to prevent them from being killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Redzic, going back to the matters I was covering in the local municipality: Were you aware of Muslim paramilitary formations in Milici in April?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware of -- just in relation to this question of the initiatives to divide the municipality, would it be true to say that the -- those initiatives, in fact, commenced towards the end of 1991 and early 1992? Would you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The formation of the institutions in Republika Srpska after a short period of time, after this happened, the desire for division in other municipalities occurred as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Redzic, of course, I'm asking you questions in relation to the local municipality of Vlasenica. You've already conceded that your knowledge at the higher level is extremely limited. Perhaps it would be more useful to concentrate on the local municipality of Vlasenica at this point. Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, during that period - February, March, and part of April 1992 - would you agree with me that a significant number of Serbs actually left the area?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with you. Children -- all the children of Serbian nationality were moved to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was not just directed to children. I'm talking about Serb people generally, not just children.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The women and people were all in the area of the municipality of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you're not agreeing with my proposition that Serb people, both male and female and children, that a significant number of Serbs left the area? You don't agree with that proposition? You're only defining it as children having left; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that that time in Vlasenica and perhaps in Bosnia generally, in early April, was a time of quite some chaos?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The events that occurred during that period of time demonstrate that it was a time of chaos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you aware of a rally, a founding rally of the SDA, in Bratunac - so we're dealing back here in 1990 - but a founding rally of the SDA in Bratunac. There were thousands of Muslims at this rally and some slogans were indicated at the rally, such as "Serbs go to Serbia and slaughter Serbs." Are you aware of anything of that nature?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're aware, of course, that the SDA banned the Muslims of Vlasenica responding to the JNA mobilisation; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not the SDA. You misconstrued the question. In response to decisions of the Presidency of the BH and of the government of the BH that followed the order, that there shouldn't be a mobilisation in Bosnia-Herzegovina. It didn't have to do with an SDA order. This was done at the level of state institutions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, of course, you're aware that that was contrary to the laws of Yugoslavia at the time; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, the problems hadn't been solved at the level of the former Yugoslavia, and it had been agreed that there shouldn't be any movement or mobilisation of troops in Bosnia-Herzegovina until the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina reached an agreement at the level of the Presidency of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, a matter of interpretation -- a matter, perhaps, of transcript. Did you say that the problem had been solved at the level of the former Yugoslavia or that it had not been solved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem hadn't been solved. The problem of going ahead with the mobilisation. The problem was to deal with this until everything had been solved at the level of the republics and the state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So, Mr. Redzic, that's your interpretation of the legality at the time, and we'll leave it at that for the time being. Now, were you aware of members of the Patriotic League in the municipality of Vlasenica in early 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. And if that had been the case, if that was in existence, I should have been aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you aware of the JNA when it left taking with it its equipment?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what people from Vlasenica said, the JNA left all its weapons and artillery in the area of the municipality of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's, of course, what you heard from other people and not something that you can give direct evidence from your own observations; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Redzic, I just want to take you back to the statement that you gave on the 12th of October, 1994, which is, of course, the first statement that you gave to the Prosecution for this institution.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Redzic might be provided by the Prosecution with a copy of his Prosecution statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I noticed that although it's on your potential exhibit list, you did not present it to the witness. Ms. Loukas, may I ask you to consider whether it will be necessary to tender it or whether it's just a specific part you want to --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, actually, there's no need to tender it, Your Honour. There are some specific aspects that I want to go to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you then take care that the relevant part is properly read into the transcript so that there's no confusion later on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Redzic, you have your statement before you; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that particular statement was taken on the 12th of October, 1994?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think you also gave a subsequent statement on the 1st of August, 2002, in which you gave further general information in relation to the municipality of Vlasenica; agreed?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when this statement was being taken, Mr. Redzic, of course, a careful note was being taken of what you were saying by the interviewers?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you understood, of course, that they needed your statement to investigate the matters that occurred in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was important for the purposes of ensuring that they could find the people responsible for what occurred in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, you understood at the time the importance of telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, of telling the whole truth?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you understood the importance of telling the Prosecution everything you knew about what had occurred in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was there, concerning the period during which I was there, from the '90s until the time that the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And, of course, the Prosecution interviewers, of course, gave you your opportunity to tell your story of what occurred; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it wasn't just a question of there being questions and answers, but you would volunteer material that you felt might assist the Prosecution; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I didn't provide them with versions of any kind. I told them the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, of course, when they asked you questions on a particular topic, you would tell them, of course, everything you knew?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was, of course, a detailed statement; you'd agree with me?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall how many hours the statement took, Mr. Redzic?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992; is that the period you're referring to, when I gave the first one?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, the Chamber is not aware of the existence of any statement of the 1st of August, 2002. We have not been provided with that. Mr. Tieger, is there any --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's not, in fact, a statement, Your Honour. It's an information report that reflects a discussion with Mr. Redzic, which covered, as counsel indicated, general information about the Vlasenica municipality. It was not the subject of -- I'd be happy to provide it to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I have is a supplemental information sheet dated the 18th of October. What I have is a supplemental information sheet dated the 30th of August, 2004. But -- so we do have some general information sheets, but not an information sheet dated the 1st of August, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry. I frankly didn't pay attention to the specific date. I understood that counsel was referring to the information reports. If there's some discrepancy, I'd be surprised, but -- it's our intention to give the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It suggests that there's a third general information sheet, information provided by this witness. Ms. Loukas, could you --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I think there may be some confusion there, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'll just locate my copy of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because you asked the witness: "And I think you also gave a subsequent statement on the 1st of August, 2002, in which you gave further general information in relation to the municipality." So I'm just wondering whether we missed something.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's just -- sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If that was dated 18th of October --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the confusion has been -- is over now. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was just referring -- all I've referred to so far is the 12th of October, 1994 statement, and that's what I'm asking the witness about. And there was that general information sheet of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 18th of October, you told us.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If I might just have a moment to check the dates of those two documents to save any confusion. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you started saying the 1st of August, 2002, and now the last time you referred to it, you said the 18th of October. We have an 18th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Both dates are in fact correct, Your Honour. The discussion or the conversation took place on the 1st of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The report was dated the 18th of October. It's the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And does that appear somewhere in the report that the interview was --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. You'll see at the top of the document the date 18 October, and then in the box beneath the heading supplemental information sheet, it indicates proofing date, Thursday, 1 August 2002. The ERN date of that document, to resolve any confusion, is 01135260.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I see. Yes. So just to enable us to not create any -- I now do understand that the 18th of October and the 1st of August are -- is the same document. Yes, please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Yes. I think it was just that question of the fact that there was two dates on that particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going back to the statement on the 12th of October, 1994, Mr. Redzic, that I was asking you questions about, the Prosecution, of course, asked you to tell them everything you knew, and you told them everything you knew at that stage; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in relation to your statement of the 12th of October, 1994, how many hours were you in conference with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But certainly it would have been most of the day, from the morning to the afternoon; you'd agree?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conversation probably took a while, but I don't remember how long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, you had a chance to read the document, your entire statement, before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe it or not, I signed it without having read it first. I trusted that what it said in the statement was correct, so there was no need for me to read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Redzic, just to clarify: Of course, you did tell the Prosecutors everything you knew at that stage; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not for me to assess how counsel wants to use her limited time, but that question has been asked and answered, I think, twice before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Loukas, in general terms, you usually take some ten minutes to find out. If you just ask the witness whether he has given to the best of his knowledge as complete as possible the answers to the questions to him, that would certainly satisfy the matters. Apart from that, asking whether he read the statement when the statement clearly says, two times, that it was read to him, that the translation was read to him orally in Bosnian, is really a waste of time. And apart from that, I know that perhaps it's part of the art of advocacy, but also questions like, did it take a considerable time? I mean, everyone who is experienced in this field of law knows that putting on paper such a statement takes a considerable time, and whether that was then four, five, or six hours, just to emphasise that, because that's -- I expect that you're going to make a point that it was either incomplete or incorrect somewhere. Just come to your point, without this introduction. And if you want to introduce that, do that in one, two, or three questions but not for ten minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I appreciate that, obviously, the jury style is very different to what is expected in front of professional Judges. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are not jurors, but I do appreciate and I do understand that it needs some adaptation. But we are only the three of us. Usually juries are more people.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Redzic, I just want to take you to some evidence you gave yesterday in court. And the page reference is page 36, for the benefit of the Court. You referred in your evidence yesterday to yourself and Mr. Stanic participating in meetings with observers every week and that on one occasion a gentleman from the monitoring mission addressed you personally and you had a conversation. Do you recall giving that evidence yesterday?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That this gentleman had had a conversation with you and also with Mr. Stanic; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've got your statement before you there, your statement of the 12th of October, 1994. You'd agree with me, would you not, Mr. Redzic, that that does not appear in your statement? I take it, to save time, the Prosecution will concede.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as the Court is aware, we filed a supplemental proofing information sheet which contained that. So I think we're all in agreement that that was not in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. With this addition, the Prosecution concedes to that, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just in relation to that, Your Honour, I don't think the supplemental proofing sheet included that there was a conversation with a gentleman from the monitoring mission. Mr. Tieger will correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you referred to that the supplemental information sheet contains seven points. Could you indicate in which one it appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Number 5, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Again, I don't think that includes the conversation with someone from a monitoring mission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed on the matter and see whether -- I do agree with you that I have some difficulty in understanding, but perhaps you can get the information from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, so you did not indicate anything in your statement about a conversation with a gentleman from the monitoring mission; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I could not remember all the details at the time. One cannot, simply cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So ten years after you gave your statement and 12 years after the events in question, your memory has improved; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. When I gave my statement, I did not mention all the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Redzic, let's go to some other evidence you gave yesterday, page 51, for the benefit of the Court and the Prosecution. Now, looking at that, you gave evidence that: "Mr. Stanic told me that there were no more possibilities and he said that these orders had come from higher up." And this was in relation to the topic of dividing the municipality. Do you recall giving that evidence yesterday, Mr. Redzic?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you have a look at your statement that you have before you. It's on page 6 in the English version. It's the paragraph commencing: "The team presented this ultimatum to a Muslim delegation."

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's just on the top of page 6 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document that Mr. Redzic has in front of him is also correspondingly numbered, so we can also refer to the numbered paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The problem is that we've got no numbers. So, therefore, it's on the top of page 6, where it says that the team presented this ultimatum. That's right on the top of page 6.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So yesterday you said in relation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that in relation to the division that Mr. Stanic told you that there were no more possibilities and he said these orders had come from higher up. If you look at your paragraph of the statement dealing with that particular issue, you indicate in the middle of the paragraph that: "The team members told us that they were given the assignment to present this ultimatum, but they did not say who had given them this task"; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says. But it must be a misunderstanding. It must be a typo or maybe a translation mistake. In any case, on very many occasions, Mr. Stanic repeated that the order came from the top, and the top is not the top of the SDA. It was well known which top he was referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you're at this stage saying that you think it was a typo; is that correct, Mr. Redzic?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. Probably I signed not having read. I trusted it was correct. This is a mistake. There may be more than this one. But I'm sure you are also clear on who was it who issued orders to the lower levels in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Redzic -- okay. So in your statement you've got they were given the assignment, did not say who gave them the task. In evidence, you say the orders came from higher up. And so it's true to say you're going higher up the ladder ten years later, correct, or attempting to?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand your question fully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll withdraw it. Was the statement read out to you, Mr. Redzic?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to October 1994?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed I am. I'm referring to the statement that's in front of you.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the time when I gave my statement and signed it in October 1994?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Loukas, I'd like --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to take your earphones off for a second. Thank you very much. Ms. Loukas, I read the statement. I read the testimony of yesterday. In your examination of the witness, you suggest, and it seems that the witness might be confused about it, that there is some contradiction between the two, which, in the view of the Chamber, and I just check with my colleagues, is not. I mean, an assignment is usually not given by your subordinates but by a higher-up level. To give a task is not something that usually you get from an equal but from someone who is above you. And the only thing he said in his testimony is that higher level, not knowing who, and to that extent the statement is fully in line with what the witness said yesterday. So you are creating a lot of confusion with the witness who might not look through that, which there should not be. If you would keep that in mind. Thank you, continue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If Your Honour takes the view that the last aspect I was covering, I'm happy to move on to the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Redzic, would you --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: There are others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I'm not -- of course, I'm not stopping you in putting questions to the witness, but I just wanted to make you aware of the -- what the Chamber noticed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going to your testimony yesterday, Mr. Redzic, at page 55, for the benefit of the Court, you indicated, at about line 20, and you were dealing with this question of people coming from Vlasenica and telling you that the soldiers and officers were very tolerant and treated the Muslim population in Vlasenica very fairly, that soldiers came and they were offered coffee and cakes. And the soldiers told them that the SDS, the Serbian Democratic Party, had requested the corps to go there, because between 300 and 350 Serbs had had their throats cut. You recall giving that evidence yesterday?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want you to have a look at your statement, the statement that's before you. And you'll recall we were at the top of page 6.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph am I looking at?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're at the top of the page on that last aspect. So not the next one, but the one after that, where you've got: "According to what people have told me, the city was entered." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think in the B/C/S version it's the paragraph that starts with the word --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's number 28 on the witness's version, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have no numbers, as I told you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you've got paragraph 28 before you, Mr. Redzic?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20? 26. No. Actually, 28. 28.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see that in that particular paragraph you're dealing with that information. Do you agree with me, about the coffee and the cakes and the soldiers and what have you?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And nowhere in that paragraph do you indicate that the SDS had requested the corps, do you, Mr. Redzic?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need for me to indicate that. We knew that there were only two parties. The SDA did not request that, so it had to be the SDS. And it would have been unnecessary to emphasise that, because the SDS was the only party that could have done that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That's your belief.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the SDS proved that with all the victims and all the misdoings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that's your belief, Mr. Redzic; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Democratic Party made us believe that with all the victims, all the destructions, that it was them who did that, and it just confirmed my belief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that's your belief, and it colours your evidence, doesn't it, Mr. Redzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. I think that's first argumentative, and the witness, secondly, cannot be expected to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Loukas, you've made your point.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going on to page 56 of your testimony yesterday, you indicate that, as part of this conversation that you were told about from people leaving Vlasenica that the soldiers said to the people: When we leave Vlasenica, it will be very difficult for you. They told them that they would leave all the weapons and artillery in Vlasenica and that is when they could expect a catastrophe. They themselves didn't know what sort of scale of conflict to expect. Do you remember giving that evidence yesterday?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can find that in paragraph 28 as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, that the soldiers said to expect a catastrophe?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Novi Sad Corps, soldiers from the Novi Sad Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Show me where in paragraph 28 it says: "When we leave Vlasenica it will be very difficult for you, and you can expect a catastrophe." Show me where it says that in paragraph 28.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll read a sentence to you: "The soldiers told us that they were surprised when Muslims greeted them and offered them coffee and cakes. When the soldiers left, they left all the equipment to the Serbs in Vlasenica, including tanks and all the other weaponry."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But nothing about: When we leave Vlasenica, it will be very difficult for you, and nothing about a catastrophe; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it doesn't imply that I'm not allowed to add subsequently what I left out from my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And ten years after you gave the statement, you have a better memory; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If that's a follow-on or a paraphrase of what the witness said, it's inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Loukas --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I withdraw it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness said that he added something he didn't tell at that time. He didn't say anything about it. But here again it's clear to this Chamber that the hearsay information he provided yesterday from what he heard from other people that were left in Vlasenica did not contain in his statement certain elements that were part of his testimony of yesterday. You made that clear to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: There's just one further matter I want to go to in relation to comparisons between the statement and the transcript, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Redzic, yesterday you told the Court Mr. Stanic always said that things were no longer in his hands, that they simply had to obey orders from higher levels, and everybody knows what higher levels were, so all the orders were handed down from higher levels to the municipal level, and at the municipal level these orders were carried out. That's at page 63, lines 14 to 18, for the benefit of the Court and the Prosecution. You remember giving that evidence yesterday, Mr. Redzic?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Show me where in your statement you indicate that Mr. Stanic was always saying to you that things were no longer in his hands and that they simply had to obey orders from higher levels. Tell me where in your statement it says that, your statement from ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it is not in the statement. However, ten years ago, when I gave my statement, I never realised that the international community would be so serious about this whole situation and that one day I would appear as a witness in this courtroom to testify about the events in Vlasenica. At that time, I did not think that all of these details were necessary. I did not believe, I couldn't hope that this problem would one day be dealt with so seriously and that I would be sitting here today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The United Nations had set up the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia when you gave your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean, these are argumentative points. Counsel can make these in closing if she wishes, but it doesn't really serve any purpose here to remind the witness that he was interviewed by representatives --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness to take his headphones off for a second. Ms. Loukas, in all investigations, you'll find that the focus will be on what is most relevant at that time. The mere fact that even if the witness would have been aware at that time that the ICTY was created, it doesn't say that specific focus on vertical lines, as we call them, and it's clear that in this case vertical lines are of major importance, that a similar focus should have been at that time already on that issue, and especially not that a witness should have been aware of the outstanding relevance of especially those issues. You made your point that the statement does not contain any information on that, but it's of no use to enter into a kind of argument with the witness whether he should have been aware at that time because the ICTY was created already, that he should have included in his answers such elements which might not even be clear to those investigators interviewing him at that time. So I do not mind at all, the Chamber does not mind that you demonstrate that there are elements in his testimony of yesterday which do not appear, but the argument you enter into with the witness is of no assistance to the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour. But I would make one point in relation to what Your Honour has just indicated. This is a witness statement that does contain questions of the chain of command, and that appears in the very first page of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not saying that it's totally absent and that no one was aware of the relevance of it, but I think I indicated that the focus on it, which does not mean that the awareness was totally absent, that vertical lines could be of some importance. And of course, I do understand that especially the chain of command was of importance, but that was -- you're referring to the bottom of page 2 and the top of page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I do not mind if you would deal with the matter, but not by putting to the witness that the awareness of the existence of the ICTY should have, well, made him more cautious in certain specific respects. So I'm not preventing you from putting questions, but it's just the way in which you do it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It's probably an appropriate juncture for a break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Some time for reflection during the break, for the Chamber as well, of course. Ms. Loukas, could you give us an indication on how much time you'd still need?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm actually just about to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would it take you to finish? Because if you say, well, I could finish in some seven minutes, then we could continue and have a break then.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I wouldn't finish in seven minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would not finish. No. Then we'll have a break now. We will -- perhaps the witness could put his headphones on again. Yes. Mr. Redzic, we'll have a break for almost half an hour. We'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Redzic, you'll be happy to know we're moving away from your statement onto another topic. Just in relation to what you've referred to in your evidence of fears that people in your local community had in relation to Muslims. I just wanted to ask you some questions about Izetbegovic. Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you're aware, of course, that on a visit to Turkey in July 1991 that Izetbegovic, Mr. Izetbegovic, asked to join the organisation of Islamic countries?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not familiar with the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are familiar, of course, that Mr. Izetbegovic asked to join the organisation of Islamic countries in 1991?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Izetbegovic stated two years before the outbreak of war that the Muslims did not yet comprise a big enough majority to make Bosnia a Muslim state? Are you aware of that statement?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not aware of that either. Okay. Were the people in your local community aware of that, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that in parliament, Mr. Izetbegovic, on February the 27th, 1991, told parliament that, and I quote: "I would sacrifice peace for a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina, but for that peace in Bosnia-Herzegovina, I would not sacrifice sovereignty." Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, superficially. But I know about someone else who said that a people would disappear from that area, and that occurred at the same session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand you've already given evidence of that, but I'm asking you about this statement, Mr. Redzic. Are you aware of whether or not people in your local community were aware of that statement by Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one could see what one could see on television, if that is what he said. It's not at all a problem, if there are public appearances, to know what was said at that session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware of a rally in Velika Kladusa -- an SDA rally in September 1990? Were you aware there was an SDA rally in Velika Kladusa in September 1990?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A pre-electoral rally before the multi-party elections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly, yes. And were you aware that there were hundreds of green flags, people in Arabic dress, and portraits of Saddam Hussein at that rally?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not, and that is incorrect. There were religious flags there, and I believe that that's not a problem of any kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you weren't aware of people chanting "long live Saddam Hussein" and "we are going to kill Vuk Draskovic"?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not personally aware of that. I wasn't present at that assembly, and I couldn't go into the details of that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that that came from the Netherlands Institute for War Documentation, would you disagree with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. The witness has clearly indicated the fact that he wasn't present at the rally, doesn't know what was said there. I'm not at all sure what the point is of getting him to discuss the contents of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, he did say that he was not personally aware because he wasn't present, and he couldn't go into the details of that matter. There seems to be an admission of some knowledge of what happened over there. Ms. Loukas, are we listening to background testimony or are we listening to anything else?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I have just one final question in relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just asking you. I mean, from the evidence we heard until [Realtime transcript read in error "not guilty"] now, it is clear that strong words might have been uttered by many people in that area and that might have some relevance to understand the background of the conflict. But, of course, this case is not about an exchange of words.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, I'm wondering, are we listening to background information to better understand that fear might have been on all sides? But again, this case is not only about fear, but also about other things that may have happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I'm wondering, is this background information or does it play a different role in the Defence position?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, of course, Your Honour, number one, it's in terms of setting context, which is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And in fact my last question to the witness will just about, to his knowledge, whether people in his community were aware of this event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Then if that's your last question, then it's not of any importance to go into further details. Please put that last question, but put it in a factual way. Because earlier when you asked the witness whether he was aware of something, then your next question was whether his people in his village were aware of that. Of course, if you are aware of the awareness of other people, that results in your own awareness as well. So therefore, the question was -- didn't make much sense. But here, perhaps you could ask the witness whether he has any reason to assume that other people were aware and what that reason would have been. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me. Before I proceed, one clarification to the transcript. On page 39, line 8, it reads: "Heard not guilty now." I believe the Court said: "Heard until now."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes it seems that I'm not speaking clearly enough to have my words properly reflected in the transcript. But I blame myself for that. Please put your last question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly, Your Honour. But I'm happy to leave it as not guilty, I must say, without correcting the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Loukas, you know that the truth is guiding us.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. Indeed I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Redzic, my final question to you is -- I'm just looking for Your Honour's formulation, Your Honour. Now, just in relation to this rally, were you aware of people in the municipality of Vlasenica being aware of this rally in Velika Kladusa?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably on the basis of what they could see on television and on the basis of what they could read in the newspapers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. No further questions, Mr. Redzic.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tieger, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi has one or more questions to you. Questioned by the Court: JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to ask you two or three minor questions. My first question is about what you called paramilitary formations in the Milici area. You said, and I quote to you in English: [In English] "Paramilitary units had already been formed at around mid-1991." [Interpretation] And further on, you said: [In English]: "Chetnik insignia." [Interpretation] Do you know who formed these units?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the leaders of the SDS parties. They did this at a higher level. And they were the founders and they formed the paramilitary units. They also acted outside the former JNA. So it was the SDS party that formed them. Because if a state institution had formed them, it would have been necessary to do this through the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina and through governmental organisations. Since this was never done at the level of the state, it was the SDS that did everything, took all steps. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] If I have understood you correctly, Mr. Stanic was elected by the SDS party as president of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Nevertheless, when you informed him about the delivery of arms to the population in the municipality, you said, and I quote you: [In English]: "Was surprised." [Interpretation] And further on you said [In English]: "...visit areas. He asked the people, and the answer was that they were afraid to be attacked by the Muslims." [Interpretation] End of quote. Please allow me to finish. Am I take to it that Mr. Stanic was surprised because he wasn't aware of the fact you said that it was the SDS that was in fact in charge of these units and of the delivery of arms, but Mr. Stanic seemed surprised. And when he was informed of the delivery of arms to the population, he seemed quite surprised. How do you reconcile these two factors? Because, on the one hand, he was a member of the SDS party, and, on the other hand, he was surprised by the fact that there were weapons delivered and there were units that existed. These units existed in the surroundings of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what I said earlier on, but I do know that Mr. Stanic was not surprised at any point in time, because he himself participated in arming the people. It was his task as the president of the Municipal Assembly and as a member of the Executive Committee of the SDS. Because he was fully informed of everything and he knew exactly which villages had to be provided with certain weapons. He knew how many weapons they needed. He knew exactly what they needed. He wasn't surprised when I visited the villages, et cetera. But I, together with him -- JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Allow me to interrupt you, Witness. You said, and I quote you: [In English] "He was surprised and asked me where I obtained this information from. [Interpretation] End of quote.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that now. The problem was that when Serbs from faraway Serbian villages came to see Stanic, Mr. Stanic wasn't in his office, and the secretary directed them to me. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation]. No. That's another issue. I'm talking about a particular incident. When you said that he was surprised to hear that the population was armed and that the population was being provided with arms. But this is something else, and you correctly said that you were taken to meet Mr. Stanic and you were told why weapons weren't being delivered. But these are two different issues, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't believe that Stanic was surprised at any point in time. He could have pretended to be surprised, but if he hadn't been aware of everything, that would have been incomprehensible. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] But Mr. Stanic was a member of the SDS party, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic was appointed by the SDS as president of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica. He was a member of the Executive Committee, of the Municipal Committee, of the Assembly Committee. I think he was a member of the Assembly at the level of the Assembly within the SDS in Republika Srpska. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. To go back to the question that I put to you, first of all, concerning the fact that he was surprised, that Mr. Stanic was surprised. Would you like to elaborate on this fact? Was he surprised by your knowledge, was he surprised by the events that were taking place, or was he surprised by the fact that you were in the know, so to speak, that you knew about this?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably because I had information from the field and I was familiar with the situation. I knew as much as he did. And it was not clear to him where such information had been obtained from. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll now move on to another subject. It has to do with a meeting you had with Mr. Stanic in private. If I have understood this correctly, you went to see him, you were alone with him, and you said that Mr. Stanic told you that it was very dangerous for him to meet you because you had already been accused by a military court. Have I understood your testimony correctly?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] You were accused or you were convicted?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An indictment was brought in October 1991. The trial was scheduled on a number of occasions, and on the 13th of December, 1992 -- 1991, I was put on trial in my absence. I was represented by counsel Balijagic. He told me I had been sentenced to ten years hard labour. I never received that document because the war then broke out, et cetera. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] You were in fact accused, you intervened to prevent a certain brigade from setting off to Kunace [phoen], in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. The Vlasenica brigade, the light brigade, which consisted of 1.200 troops, 80 per cent of them were Muslims, Bosniaks, this brigade was mobilised, although it didn't have the right to be mobilised because the Presidency of Yugoslavia and the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina hadn't reached an agreement. They mobilised the troops, took them to Han Pijesak, and then transported them to Zaluzani near Banja Luka, and they were supposed to be transported to Slavonija, to Vukovar and to Okucani and to Osijek from there. I left with six or seven lorries with women and children, and I returned 90 per cent of those troops from Zaluzani to Vlasenica. And naturally, from Banja Luka, I had to engage, I had to get hold of about ten new buses. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] But you represent the civilian authority, you represented the civilian authority, and this brigade was under military orders. It was directed and had to obey military orders?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But at that time, the army didn't have the competence to mobilise in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Not up until the time that an agreement was reached at the level of the former Yugoslavia and at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
